recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for FHIR-17428. No further core source action is needed for the Dosage datatype unless a future editorial pass chooses to clean up the harmless double space left by the 2018 application.
issue_request: FHIR-17428 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core pharm change request for STU3 asking that Dosage.timing requirements stop naming the obsolete Schedule datatype and instead refer generically to this datatype.
initial_application: The Jira comment records the change as applied in July 2018, and git history confirms commit ce698b9ee5288dac0d1f13735b92bb16a46c008d changed source/datatypes/dosage.xml from "The Schedule data type allows many different expressions" to "This  data type allows many different expressions".
additional_context: Dosage remains an active datatype in source/fhir.ini, and the current source/datatypes/dosage.xml Dosage.timing row has type Timing and no longer mentions Schedule in the requirements sentence. Quoted Zulip and Confluence searches for FHIR-17428 plus Dosage/Schedule/Timing found no community record that changes the Jira/source conclusion. A separate current DeviceRequest occurrence of similar Schedule wording was observed, but the Jira fields and implementation commit for FHIR-17428 are scoped to the Dosage datatype, so that separate artifact was not decided here.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch because the active current Dosage source already satisfies FHIR-17428.
